h: Making a Night of It in Devon's Capital
p: Exeter is one of those cities that feels just the right size. It's big enough to have plenty going on, with a university, a busy shopping centre and a lively evening scene, but small enough to walk across in an afternoon. That makes it ideal for a group night out, especially if you're coming in from the towns and villages around Devon.

Exeter St Davids is the main station, with direct trains from London, Bristol and the rest of the South West, and Exeter Central is closer to the shops. If you're driving, the park and ride sites are worth considering, as city-centre parking can be pricey at busy times.

For a games night with a group, a little planning helps. Book ahead, especially on Fridays and Saturdays in term time, and give everyone a time to arrive. Mix up the teams so no one side is stacked with the competitive ones, and make sure the scores are visible so the rivalry stays alive.

With a day to spare, you're spoiled for choice. Dartmoor is a short drive west, with wild moorland, tors and rivers that feel a million miles from the city. Exmouth and its long sandy beach are reachable by train along the Exe estuary, which is a lovely ride in its own right. Closer to home, Powderham Castle sits on the estuary just outside the city, with a deer park and a long history as the home of the Earls of Devon.
